speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Notwithstanding this, if I can presume to read into Ms Lim's underlying concern, it is indeed something that the Ministry of Education (MOE) is focused upon because it is important that the students from the lower SES homes are able to overcome their circumstances and do well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Our efforts to support the learning of students who need more help are working.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE has put in place various programmes to provide additional support targeted at specific learning needs of students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We have a special reading programme for Kindergarten 2 children with difficulties learning English; and the Learning Support Programme in English and Mathematics for Primary 1 and Primary 2 students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: At the higher grade levels, there are corresponding programmes such as those that provide reading remediation or help students improve their confidence and numeracy skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Other efforts include targeted needs-based financial assistance schemes across all schooling years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: But we do not rest on our laurels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: It takes constant hard work to enable every student to achieve their potential during their educational journey, especially those from more challenging home circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE will therefore continue to work closely with other agencies and community partners to provide the necessary support for students who need it most.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, he mentioned that my assumption in the question was not correct.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But from the report, it is stated that Belgium, Singapore and Switzerland were the only three high-performing countries with below-average levels of equity in education outcome.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The only three high-performing countries with below-average levels of equity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, is that not an indication that we have a bigger issue to worry about in terms of equity?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State is, what indicators does MOE track of social mobility in education?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In a previous Parliamentary Question (PQ) that I filed almost 10 years ago, we know from the then Minister that MOE does track, for example, students going to our public universities based on housing type.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We had an indication of social mobility there but are there any other indicators that the Ministry tracks internally?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would be happy to follow up with Ms Lim or she can file a separate PQ on internal data.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The information I have is related to the OECD report and I would like to address the first question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But our higher SES students outperform the higher SES students in other OECD countries by an even larger margin resulting in the differential that she talked about.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, our lower SES students are doing well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Our lower SES students are outperforming the OECD average.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, it does not mean that our lower SES students are under-performing their OECD counterparts.
